card.statement:
Let $\mathscr{C}$ be an abelian $\mathbf{k}$ -linear category and let
$\omega:\mathscr{C}\to{\mathord{\mathrm{Vect}}}_{\mathbf{k}}$ be a $\mathbf{k}$ -linear exact faithful functor.
Fix an object $X$ in $\mathscr{C}$ and introduce the finite-dimensional
$\mathbf{k}$ -algebra

$A_{X}:=\bigl\{\alpha\in\End_{\mathbf{k}}(\omega(X))\bigm|\forall n\geq 0,\ \forall Y\subset X^{\oplus n}\ \text{subobject},\ \alpha^{\oplus n}(\omega(Y))\subset\omega(Y)\bigr\}.$

Then $\omega\bigl|_{\langle X\rangle}$ admits a canonical factorization

$\textstyle{\langle X\rangle\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$ $\scriptstyle{\overline{\omega}_{X}}$ $\scriptstyle{\omega}$ $\textstyle{{\mathord{\mathrm{Mod}}}_{A_{X}}\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces\ignorespaces}$ $\scriptstyle{{\mathord{\mathrm{forget}}}}$ $\textstyle{{\mathord{\mathrm{Vect}}}_{\mathbf{k}},}$

and $\overline{\omega}_{X}$ is an equivalence of categories.
In addition $A_{X}$ is the endomorphism algebra of the functor
$\omega\bigl|_{\langle X\rangle}$ .

If $A$ is a $\mathbf{k}$ -algebra, and if we apply this proposition to the
category $\mathscr{C}={\mathord{\mathrm{Mod}}}_{A}$ of finite-dimensional $A$ -modules with $\omega$ the forgetful functor (which
keeps the $\mathbf{k}$ -vector space structure but forgets the structure of
$A$ -module), then Exercise 2.1 shows that the algebra $A_{X}$
is precisely the image of $A$ in $\End_{\mathbf{k}}(X)$ . The proposition is thus
mainly saying that the exercise can be stated within the language
of abelian categories.

For the proof of Proposition 2.2 we will need the following standard facts from Category Theory.
card.label: Proposition 2.2

paper.title: Notes on the geometric Satake equivalence
paper.abstract: These notes are devoted to a detailed exposition of the proof of the Geometric Satake Equivalence for general coefficients, following Mirkovic-Vilonen.
